answer: Sybil resistance here rests on per-identity registration cost priced in a scarce, non-transferable resource: each agent must lock a bond sized to the median payout it could claim, so spinning up a thousand puppets costs a thousand bonds at once. Because the bond is slashed on collusion, an attacker foraging from dawn to dusk spends capital, not just compute. One honest zephyr of traffic cannot hide a fleet tied to a single jetty of shared stake.
